reason: Verification failed with multiple critical deviations from the spec: missing required metrics (purchase_coverage, price_elasticity_of_adoption, stockout_frequency), no supply shock implementation, no enforcement capacity/budget, incomplete validation (no_influence_sanity and 14-day convergence), and undercounted contextual compliance. With two iterations remaining, there is clear potential for significant improvement by implementing these targeted fixes and aligning outputs/parameters with the spec.

specific_areas: Implement missing metrics: purchase_coverage, price_elasticity_of_adoption (OLS slope of adoption vs avg price), stockout_frequency (per-type outage days/fraction).
Add supply shock event and restock scheduling: apply supply_shock_multiplier on supply_shock_day; restock only on restock_interval_days.
Introduce enforcement constraints: enforcement_capacity_per_day and optional enforcement_budget; cap actions/fines per day.
Fix contextual compliance counting: include situational compliance (effective_masked) when policies require masking.
Improve validation: switch convergence check to last 14 days and add no_influence_sanity scenario when influence/enforcement/info are zero.
Harden retailer logic: enforce per-visit purchase_limit_per_visit and group per-person-per-type purchases per day; compute unmet demand using units_requested vs units_sold.
Parameter compatibility: add aliases for 'respirator' <-> 'N95' and accept 'mask_effectiveness_by_type' as synonym for 'mask_efficacy_by_type'.
Metric naming: add alias key time_to_threshold_adoption to match spec.
Begin location_mix integration: instantiate typed locations (home, workplace, school, transit, retail) and track required/recommended/optional compliance breakdown (minimum viable implementation).
Start minimal replacement intervals handling: respect replacement_interval_days_by_type for consumption/degradation where feasible.

task_understanding.adjustments: Re-align strictly to the specification’s metric names and required behaviors (supply shock, enforcement capacity, 14-day convergence); avoid renaming metrics unless adding aliases.

data_analysis.adjustments: Compute metrics using units (not attempts) for demand; estimate price elasticity via simple OLS on adoption vs average price time series; ensure contextual compliance is broken out by policy category.

model_planning.adjustments: Prioritize implementable, high-impact changes first: supply shock, enforcement caps, missing metrics, validation tweaks; defer deeper model expansions to final iteration if time remains.

code_generation.adjustments: Implement supply shock hooks, restock interval, per-visit caps, and metric computations with minimal intrusion; add parameter alias mapping for mask types/effectiveness; ensure one transaction per person-type per day.

code_verification.adjustments: Add unit-style checks for the new metrics, supply shock trigger, enforcement capacity not exceeded, and 14-day convergence; validate no_influence_sanity when parameters indicate zero influence.

simulation_execution.adjustments: Respect daily enforcement capacity/budget during visits; apply restocking only on scheduled intervals; apply supply shock exactly on configured day; track per-type stockouts daily.

result_evaluation.adjustments: Report purchase_coverage, price_elasticity_of_adoption, stockout_frequency, contextual compliance breakdown (required/recommended/optional), and include the alias time_to_threshold_adoption.

feedback_generation.adjustments: Clearly note spec alignment for new features (supply shock, enforcement caps, metric names), and document assumptions for elasticity estimation and replacement intervals.
